title: T3 live conversation checklist
purpose: Exercise complete observable T3 conversation workflows with the authorized Sol and Sonnet providers, then compare the actual behavior to direct source symbols. This is an execution plan, not a runtime findings report.
scope: fork, side chat, reopen and persistence
ownership: Parent alone controls native T3, model tasks, fixture creation, runtime evidence and cleanup. This worker performed read-only source investigation and wrote these two documents. No UI control, model calls, application launches, builds, tests or additional agents.
source_runtime_rule: Record the installed build/version first. If it differs from the pinned commit, retain the discrepancy and resolve the actual observed behavior against the corresponding source before attributing a defect.

principles_applied.Experience First: Each case begins with an actual user action and visible outcome, including ordinary input and return paths.
principles_applied.Prove It Works: All result slots start not-run. Source, widgets, helper tests and model acknowledgements are not interchangeable evidence.
principles_applied.Sequence Work into Verifiable Units: Three linked task bundles create reusable states; each case has its own assertions and cleanup.

runtime_result_states.passed-bounded: The specified action, assertion and return path were observed for this provider, with evidence. Does not certify unlisted branches or the whole surface.
runtime_result_states.failed-reproduced: An actual live action and its wrong result are evidenced and confounds have been addressed.
runtime_result_states.inconclusive: The input, render, provider or ownership boundary could not be established.
runtime_result_states.not-available-with-observed-reason: The runtime shows the capability/action is unavailable for the installed provider/account/build, with the actual reason captured.
runtime_result_states.not-reached: The bounded real task did not create the required state; no success or defect is inferred.

completion_rule: A case is not passed by source existence, a visible control, a screenshot of an idle surface, a helper unit test or a result from the other provider. Capture the entry action, real outcome, source match and recovery/return. Split mixed results instead of promoting the whole case.

sonnet.model: Claude Sonnet (record exact authorized installed variant)

shared.sol: Verify the selected Sol thread identity and actual visible action; a shared widget does not establish provider delivery.
shared.sonnet: Repeat the shared interaction in the Sonnet lane and record its identity. A Sol pass is not a Sonnet pass.

send.sol: Verify a real Sol turn receives the distinct text, citation and attachment markers applicable to this case once. Model acknowledgement is semantic evidence, not byte-exact transport evidence.
send.sonnet: Verify a real Sonnet turn receives the corresponding markers once; Claude attachment conversion and history differ from Codex. Do not inherit a Sol delivery result.

stream.sol: Codex declares assistant, reasoning, tool and plan streaming. Require an intermediate visible update before completion for each output type actually exercised.
stream.sonnet: Claude declares assistant/reasoning streaming but not generic tool/plan streaming. Its separate tailClaudeTaskOutput path may supply live background command output. Record first, intermediate and final observations for the actual path instead of declaring all tool output unavailable.

queue.sol: Codex supports queueing, active turn/steer and interruption. Prove exact marker identity, cardinality and order at the exercised transition.
queue.sonnet: Claude supports queueing and active steering; steering may interrupt tools and background foreground subagents. Check the visible owner, accepted prompt and resulting work. No assumption of Codex interruption behavior.

permissions.sol: Set Supervised before the task and inspect the actual request. Codex maps supervised execution to approval-required policy; distinguish Approve, Decline and Cancel and observe the tool outcome.
permissions.sonnet: Start the task in Supervised because Claude cannot change runtime mode within a native session. Observe the real permission request and response, not merely a changed menu label. Session grants must not leak beyond owned work.

questions.sol: Require actual structured requestUserInput and verify question IDs, required options/free text and the submitted answer. Prose questions are not a pass.
questions.sonnet: Require AskUserQuestion through canUseToolEffect or a real elicitation through onElicitationEffect. Exercise the actual schema and returned answers; a prose question or unrelated approval does not satisfy this branch.

agents.sol: Codex exposes native child IDs, snapshots, waits, close and child fork capabilities. Prove the correct child/parent IDs and live content, with the authorized model recorded.
agents.sonnet: Claude does not declare native child thread IDs, native snapshot/child fork or child approvals, but the app projects child work and stopSubagent can call a live owning query. Verify the observed projected/read-only surface and stop result rather than assuming the Codex model.

fork.sol: Codex supports root, turn and child forks and rollback. Verify the actual selected boundary and parent isolation, not just a new thread title.
fork.sonnet: Claude supports root/turn forks and rollback via its transcript path, not native child forks. Verify which boundary is available and whether the source history is preserved.

restore.sol: Verify editable draft/history restoration using real navigation or a normal restart after work is quiescent. Codex native snapshot support is not proof of UI restore; live-only pending callbacks do not survive restart.
restore.sonnet: Verify the actual transcript/side-chat and editable draft after restore. Claude does not declare native snapshots or restart-surviving pending requests; record clean recovery or explicit unavailable state, not invented continuity.

label_rule: Static action labels are copied from the pinned source. ${...} denotes a dynamic source label template, not literal UI text. Descriptive catalog entries explicitly tell the operator to record the actual label. Installed custom keymaps and provider-specific approval options override generic defaults.

scratch_fixture_manifest.requirements: Harmless Markdown with FILE_MARKER_T3, TOOL_FIND_SENTINEL, a table/headings and at least 120 numbered lines; include no secrets or instructions to act on unrelated work.
Small readable function with a known source-line target and no external side effects.
Small image with a known visible marker. Parent creates and inspects it before the task; record its dimensions.
Tiny distinct scratch images for image-strip overflow and previous/next preview.
Initially absent. Only the deliberately approved bundle B action creates or changes it.

task_bundles.title: Read, render, cite and control a running turn
task_bundles.prompt: Work only in this disposable audit scratch project. Do not spawn subagents or access unrelated files. Read audit-notes.md and audit-code.py, and inspect the attached audit image. First give an interim report with STREAM_START_T3, the FILE_MARKER_T3 value, the visible image marker, 24 numbered observations, a small table, a Python code fence with a long line, a literal blockquote, a relative link to audit-code.py and a harmless https://example.com link. Then run exactly one foreground local command that emits TICK_T3_01 through TICK_T3_36, one every five seconds, with an absolute 180-second bound. Do not detach, daemonize or restart it after interruption unless explicitly instructed. This command is for observing output and turn controls. After it ends, give a short final report ending FINAL_T3_A. Do not change files, use network tools or launch background processes.
execution_notes: Run the pre-send intake cases first. Use the bounded command window for live/scroll and queue actions; remove unused queue entries before automatic continuation.

All UI case checks need not fit one 180-second window. If a state expires, mark the branch not-reached or deliberately request one separately recorded bounded continuation. Never leave the task running indefinitely to complete a checklist.
Queue and citation acknowledgements, if sent, are additional actual turns. Keep them short and record them; three bundles do not mean only three provider calls.
Repeat the provider-dependent send, stream, queue, steer and stop paths on Sonnet. Shared UI results still require evidence in each claimed lane.

task_bundles.title: Exercise decisions, native child work and lineage
task_bundles.prompt: Work only in this disposable audit scratch project using the selected authorized model. Use your real structured question tool, if available, for two questions: choose ALPHA or BETA, and provide a short free-text marker. Do not imitate a structured question with prose; say plainly if the tool is unavailable. Then request the harmless creation of audit-write.txt containing the chosen markers, respecting any approval or denial. For a second approval trial, request a harmless scratch-only printf and do not retry it if denied. Create at most two descendants in total: one child named T3-AUDIT-CHILD to read and summarize audit-code.py, and, only if supported, one grandchild named T3-AUDIT-GRANDCHILD to read audit-notes.md. Use the same authorized model for descendants where configurable and report actual model choices. No further descendants. Keep each summary under 150 words. A child may run one foreground tick command bounded to 90 seconds for observing its live view; never detach it. Report the real child identifiers. Finish only when all owned work is completed or explicitly stopped.
execution_notes: Set Supervised before starting the native session. A label changed mid-session does not prove effective Claude permission changes.
Model compliance is not guaranteed. Record absent question/approval/child states honestly and distinguish native capabilities from application projections.
If the selected provider cannot honor the child model restriction, record the observed model or avoid launching that child. Do not silently substitute a more expensive model.
Keep a descendant ledger and use real Stop actions before independent liveness cleanup.

task_bundles.title: Use completed histories to verify recovery and return paths
task_bundles.prompt: This is a bounded audit recovery check on the selected fork or side chat. In fewer than 80 words, acknowledge the supplied source marker and identify which conversation context you received. Do not use tools, edit files, create agents or start background work. End with RECOVERY_T3_C.
execution_notes: Reuse bundle A/B histories; no new long task is required. At most one short fork reply and one short side-chat reply per provider are planned, with any extra acknowledgement or fresh-session turn counted separately.
Rewind only a disposable owned fork. File rollback must be restricted to known scratch checkpoints.
Normal app restart belongs to the parent after all owned work is settled and unrelated work is safe. Do not use abrupt termination as a substitute for normal restore.
Close/reopen applies to surviving side-chat surfaces. It is not a claim that deleted arbitrary root threads can be reopened.

cases.title: Identify the actual build, provider, model, effort and permissions
actions: Record installed T3 build/version and compare it with the pinned commit. Record the active project, checkout, account/provider, exact model display name, effort and permission label.
Open and dismiss the model, effort and permissions menus with mouse and keyboard; inspect any customized shortcuts before relying on defaults.
success_assertions: Sol and Sonnet are the explicitly authorized models, with no silent fallback.
Selection persists into the task and the visible thread identifies the same provider. A disabled or missing authorized model has a recorded reason.
cases.restore_and_cleanup: Save the original configuration and window/panel sizes for restoration; do not alter unrelated threads.

Delete one citation, undo the deletion, and edit the second comment.
success_assertions: Text insertion, delete/undo and comment editing preserve each citation/source pairing. No unrelated general text or second citation is lost.
cases.restore_and_cleanup: Remove exploratory citations or keep only the intended next prompt.

provider_assertions.sol: Verify the selected Sol thread identity and actual visible action; a shared widget does not establish provider delivery.
provider_assertions.sonnet: Repeat the shared interaction in the Sonnet lane and record its identity. A Sol pass is not a Sonnet pass.

cases.title: Exercise citation and comment length boundaries honestly
actions: If the real response is long enough, select more than 8000 characters and inspect Shorten selection, then shorten to an accepted selection.
In a comment editor try 8001 characters, inspect Shorten comment, then reduce to 8000 and cancel after verifying readiness.
success_assertions: Oversized content has an explicit non-sending state; accepted content can be edited without truncation. The source selection branch remains not-reached when the available response is too short, instead of generating artificial evidence.
cases.restore_and_cleanup: Cancel the boundary comment and remove the oversized selection; do not send the oversized fixture.

provider_assertions.sol: Verify the selected Sol thread identity and actual visible action; a shared widget does not establish provider delivery.

cases.title: Keep literal blockquote text distinct from a citation through restore
actions: Prepare a draft containing a literal leading > line, ordinary prose, a real citation and a fixture attachment. Stash/restore and navigate away/back.
Recheck after the later normal restart, then edit the literal line and citation comment separately.
success_assertions: Plain text formatting remains editable as text, while intentional citations preserve their source identity. No extra citation tile or silent literal-text loss appears.
cases.restore_and_cleanup: Preserve the draft only until the recovery evidence is complete, then clear owned content.

provider_assertions.sol: Verify editable draft/history restoration using real navigation or a normal restart after work is quiescent. Codex native snapshot support is not proof of UI restore; live-only pending callbacks do not survive restart.
provider_assertions.sonnet: Verify the actual transcript/side-chat and editable draft after restore. Claude does not declare native snapshots or restart-surviving pending requests; record clean recovery or explicit unavailable state, not invented continuity.

cases.title: Reply to a whole response without losing the user annotation
actions: Use Reply to this response on a known assistant response. Inspect the inserted response context and add WHOLE_REPLY_T3 as general text.
Send a short acknowledgement request and inspect the sent representation.
success_assertions: The response context and the user annotation both reach the intended turn once. The context can be identified from the composer and sent row.
cases.restore_and_cleanup: Record the extra short turn and leave no unintended reply context in the composer.

provider_assertions.sol: Verify a real Sol turn receives the distinct text, citation and attachment markers applicable to this case once. Model acknowledgement is semantic evidence, not byte-exact transport evidence.
provider_assertions.sonnet: Verify a real Sonnet turn receives the corresponding markers once; Claude attachment conversion and history differ from Codex. Do not inherit a Sol delivery result.

actions: Use explicit parent/fork/side links and the installed back/forward navigation through the known owned surfaces. At each stop inspect title, ID, model, draft and reading position.
success_assertions: Each transition reaches the intended conversation and keeps its own state. Returning does not exchange drafts, show a different agent history or unexpectedly start work.
cases.restore_and_cleanup: End on the original user surface after all audit-owned views are closed.

provider_assertions.sol: Verify editable draft/history restoration using real navigation or a normal restart after work is quiescent. Codex native snapshot support is not proof of UI restore; live-only pending callbacks do not survive restart.
provider_assertions.sonnet: Verify the actual transcript/side-chat and editable draft after restore. Claude does not declare native snapshots or restart-surviving pending requests; record clean recovery or explicit unavailable state, not invented continuity.

cases.title: Read and export an actual proposed plan
actions: If a real proposed-plan card is emitted, expand/collapse it, search within its content, then use Plan actions to copy and download it.
Use Save to workspace only for an owned scratch destination and inspect the resulting file.
success_assertions: Plan content stays readable and exported content matches the displayed plan. A generic Markdown answer is not substituted for the real plan-card route.
cases.restore_and_cleanup: Remove only audit plan exports after retaining evidence; leave the branch not-reached if no real card was emitted.

provider_assertions.sol: Verify the selected Sol thread identity and actual visible action; a shared widget does not establish provider delivery.
provider_assertions.sonnet: Repeat the shared interaction in the Sonnet lane and record its identity. A Sol pass is not a Sonnet pass.

cases.title: Record conditional voice and compaction states without inventing availability
actions: Inspect voice availability and its actual setup/disabled reason. If already configured, start and cancel an owned short input, then inspect the draft.
If Compact and send appears during real bounded work, inspect its effect on the intended draft and turn; do not manufacture token exhaustion to force it.
success_assertions: Cancel voice input stops capture and preserves intended draft content. Compaction, if reached, sends the intended prompt once with truthful state. Unavailable and not-reached branches remain distinct from passes.
cases.restore_and_cleanup: End any owned recording and restore the starting composer state.

provider_assertions.sol: Verify the selected Sol thread identity and actual visible action; a shared widget does not establish provider delivery.
provider_assertions.sonnet: Repeat the shared interaction in the Sonnet lane and record its identity. A Sol pass is not a Sonnet pass.

cases.title: Finish with no owned work or accidental queue left behind
actions: Enumerate all audit root/fork/side/child/grandchild IDs and model turns. Remove every unused queued item, resolve or cancel requests, stop owned running work and verify bounded commands are no longer alive.
Close owned views and browser tabs, remove audit stash/drafts/uploads, and restore original model/permission/panel/focus settings.
success_assertions: Every started audit task is accounted for as completed or stopped. No owned command, recording, queued turn, pending request or child is left running. Only audit-owned objects are archived/deleted under the parent authorized cleanup scope.
cases.restore_and_cleanup: Retain screenshots, result records and source links. Report any remaining owned object explicitly rather than hiding a cleanup failure.

source_boundaries.meaning: These are source constants, not tested limits. Only the listed bounded trials can gain runtime results.

evidence_record_required: installed build/version and source revision match
exact visible entry label and actual configured shortcut
visible text/result and optional independently observed provider/native event
direct source path and owning symbol

execution_accounting.model_invocations: Count every real submit, queued delivery, steer, fork reply, side-chat reply and descendant. Bundles are not token or invocation limits.
execution_accounting.model_scope: Use only the user-authorized Sol and Sonnet choices; record exact variants and any unavailable account/model state.
execution_accounting.task_bound: Bound each scratch command and descendant; do not leave tasks running while inspecting static surfaces.
execution_accounting.cleanup: Parent owns all runtime teardown and must identify every started audit thread/process.
